meta.title: 一副牌要洗幾次才算洗好
meta.subtitle: 同一副撲克牌，換一種距離就換一個答案：五次、七次、十二次
meta.summary: 52 張牌分成兩疊、交錯落下（鴿尾式）洗七次，與均勻分佈的全變異距離是 0.334。這個數字的意思是：拿洗過的牌和電腦排的隨機牌各一副放在你面前，就算用最會挑毛病的方法去檢查，也只有 66.7% 的把握指出哪一副洗過，瞎猜是 50%。改用資訊量衡量，洗五次剩 3.52% 的資訊；只在意紅黑，第六次的分離距離是 0.317；要讓全副牌序在分離距離下收斂，洗十二次仍有 0.278。文內的精確表由本站以整數有理數重算，與 Bayer–Diaconis 1992 年的原表相符。

en.title: How many shuffles does a deck need
en.subtitle: One deck of cards: change the distance and the answer changes to five, seven or twelve
en.summary: Seven riffle shuffles (split the deck in two, let the packets fall interleaved) leave a 52-card deck 0.334 away from uniform in total variation. Put that deck beside one a computer arranged at random: even the shrewdest check anyone can run identifies the shuffled one only 66.7 percent of the time, against 50 percent for a guess. Measured by information, 3.52 percent survives five shuffles; for colours alone the separation distance is 0.317 by the sixth; the full order is still 0.278 away after twelve. The exact table here was recomputed in exact integer arithmetic and agrees with the 1992 original.

split-example.title: 一次洗牌拆兩段，兩次拆四段
split-example.description: 十二張牌的分步例子。切牌把照順序排好的牌分成兩堆，交錯落下時每堆內部的前後次序不動，所以洗一次之後整副最多兩段遞增序列；第二次切牌把每一段最多再拆成兩段。洗 $k$ 次的牌堆最多 $2^k$ 段。
split-example.notes: order1 是把 1–6 與 7–12 兩堆交錯的一種合法落法（兩堆各自的相對次序保持），遞增序列數 2：{1–6}、{7–12}。order2 是把 order1 的前六張 [1,7,2,8,9,3] 與後六張 [4,10,5,11,6,12] 再交錯的一種合法落法，遞增序列數 4：{1–3}、{4–6}、{7–9}、{10–12}——原來的每一段各被拆成兩段。兩個排列都是手選的定值，不是抽樣，選它是因為每段恰好對半、段數正好走滿上限 1→2→4。

rising-sequences.title: 洗過的牌會留下痕跡：遞增序列
rising-sequences.description: 一副依序排好的 52 張牌，按 Gilbert–Shannon–Reeds 模型連續洗牌。滑桿選洗牌次數，每張牌依它所屬的遞增序列上色。洗 k 次之後，牌堆最多只能被切成 $2^k$ 段遞增序列；均勻隨機的牌堆平均有 26.5 段，標準差 2.10，落在 16 段以內的機率是 $4.67 \times 10^{-7}$。四次以下的牌堆因此連「看起來像隨機」都做不到。
rising-sequences.notes: GSR 正向模型：先依二項分佈 $\mathrm{Bin}(n, 1/2)$ 決定切牌位置，左右兩堆各剩 A 與 B 張時，下一張來自左堆的機率為 $A/(A+B)$。遞增序列的計數方式：把牌堆由上而下讀成一個排列，原始牌值連號且在牌堆中順序遞增的極大區段各算一段；等價於 $r = d(\pi^{-1}) + 1$，$d$ 為下降位置數。均勻分佈下 $r$ 的分佈由 Eulerian 數給出，平均 $(n+1)/2 = 26.5$。亂數產生器為 mulberry32，種子 20260812，與 data/reference/card-shuffling.json 的參考輸出同一套算法。

mixing-curve.title: 全變異距離的下墜：cutoff
mixing-curve.description: 每種牌堆大小各畫一條曲線：洗 k 次之後的分佈與均勻分佈之間的全變異距離。距離先貼著 1 不動，到某一點才開始下墜，之後每洗一次大約減半。虛線標出 $\frac{3}{2}\log_2 n$。52 張牌的第 5 次是 0.924、第 6 次 0.614、第 7 次 0.334、第 8 次 0.167。
mixing-curve.notes: 由 Bayer–Diaconis 定理 1 精確計算，以整數有理數（BigInt）算到底，數值由資料倉產出、前端只排版，不涉及亂數，不需要 seed。洗 k 次後排列 $\pi$ 的機率為 $\binom{2^k + n - r}{n} / 2^{kn}$，$r$ 為 $\pi$ 的遞增序列數；全變異距離 $= \frac{1}{2}\sum_r A(n,r)\,\bigl|\binom{2^k+n-r}{n}/2^{kn} - 1/n!\bigr|$，$A(n,r)$ 為 Eulerian 數。七種牌堆大小、k 從 1 到 10 共 70 個數值，與原文表 3（p.309）全部相符。

guessing-game.title: 把距離換成猜中的張數
guessing-game.description: 牌背朝上逐張猜，猜完翻開再猜下一張。均勻隨機的牌堆，最佳策略平均猜中 $H_{52} = 4.54$ 張。原文用同一個策略跑 Monte Carlo，每個數字十萬次，洗五次仍多猜中兩張，洗六次剩一張，之後每次大約減半。

series.cut: 洗 k 次後再切一次牌

guessing-game.notes: 兩列數值照錄 Bayer–Diaconis 表 5（p.310），每個數字基於十萬次模擬，策略是該文 5.1 節描述的猜法（原文稱其為推測的最佳策略，最佳性未證明）。基準線 4.538 為 $H_{52} = \sum_{i=1}^{52} 1/i$ 的精確值，原文正文寫作 4.54。本圖只排版母本數值，不在瀏覽器重跑模擬。

question-panel.title: 換一個問題，答案就不同
question-panel.description: 同一套洗牌、同一個分離距離，五種問法各畫一條線。問全副牌序的排列，洗十二次仍有 0.278；只問二十一點看得見的牌值，第九次就掉到 0.366；只問紅黑，第六次 0.317。
question-panel.notes: 五列照錄 Assaf–Diaconis–Soundararajan 表 1（arXiv:0908.3462v1, p.3）。距離為分離距離 $\mathrm{sep}(P) = \max_w \bigl(1 - P(w)/U(w)\bigr)$，與 mixing-curve 圖的全變異距離不同，兩張圖的縱軸不可互相比較；分離距離恆不小於全變異距離。第一列由 Bayer–Diaconis 公式精確計算，其餘四列為該文的近似公式，原文說明紅黑列在 k=1,2 與 Conger–Viswanath 的精確值 0.8898、0.8897 有差距。

trefethen2000.container: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 456(2002): 2561–2568
trefethen2000.locator: p.2564 圖 2 的說明文字與同頁正文：改以資訊量衡量時沒有 cut-off，$\log_2 n$ 次就把資訊降到任意小的比例。

quiz.prompt: 「52 張牌要洗七次」這句話，最準確的讀法是哪一個？
options: 洗到第七次，牌堆就成了均勻隨機的排列
第六次還完全不隨機，到第七次才變隨機
七次是實驗量出來的經驗值，沒有算式支撐
洗到第七次，全變異距離降到 0.334，最會挑毛病的檢查也只有 66.7% 認得出哪一副洗過
quiz.explain: 52 張牌的距離第七次是 0.334，第八次 0.167，第十次 0.043，一直往下，永遠不到 0。七這個數字站在曲線陡降的那一段（第五次到第八次），沒有哪一次跨過一條界線。全變異距離取的是所有事件裡的最大差距，所以 0.334 說的是：把洗過的牌和隨機排的牌擺在一起，最好的那套檢查認出洗過那一副的機率是 $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} \times 0.334 = 66.7\%$，瞎猜是 50%。

en.prompt: Which reading of “a 52-card deck needs seven shuffles” is the accurate one?
options: After the seventh shuffle the deck is a uniformly random permutation
The sixth shuffle leaves the deck ordered and the seventh makes it random
Seven is an experimental figure with no formula behind it
After seven shuffles the distance is 0.334, so even the shrewdest check spots the shuffled deck only 67% of the time
en.explain: For 52 cards the distance runs 0.334 at seven shuffles, 0.167 at eight, 0.043 at ten — always falling, never zero. Seven sits inside the steep stretch of the curve, between the fifth and eighth shuffle; no single shuffle crosses a line. Total variation takes the largest gap over all events, so 0.334 says this: set the shuffled deck beside a randomly arranged one and the best check available picks out the shuffled deck with probability $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} \times 0.334 = 66.7\%$.

quiz.prompt: 為什麼洗四次以下的牌堆，連「看起來像隨機」都做不到？
options: 洗四次還動不到最底下那幾張牌
洗 k 次至多有 $2^k$ 段遞增序列，四次至多 16 段，隨機牌堆平均 26.5 段
四次還不到 $\frac{3}{2}\log_2 52 = 8.55$ 次
切牌位置服從二項分佈，洗四次還沒攤平
quiz.explain: 每洗一次，遞增序列的段數至多加倍，四次至多 16 段。均勻分佈下段數平均 $(n+1)/2 = 26.5$、標準差 2.10，落在 16 段以內的機率是 $4.67 \times 10^{-7}$，大約兩百萬次才遇得到一次。數段數這一個檢驗就把四次以下的牌堆和隨機牌堆分開了，而且幾乎不會判錯，前四次的全變異距離因此是 1.000。8.55 是漸近公式給出的位置，四次不夠的理由是段數數得出來。

en.prompt: Why does a deck shuffled four times or fewer fail even to look random?
options: Four shuffles never reach the cards at the bottom
$k$ shuffles leave at most $2^k$ rising sequences, so at most 16 after four, against 26.5 on average for a random deck
Four is short of $\frac{3}{2}\log_2 52 = 8.55$
The cut position is binomial, and four shuffles have not flattened it
en.explain: Each shuffle at most doubles the number of rising sequences, so four give at most 16. Under the uniform distribution the count averages $(n+1)/2 = 26.5$ with standard deviation 2.10, and lands at 16 or below with probability $4.67 \times 10^{-7}$ — about once in two million decks. Counting rising sequences, one test on its own, separates a four-shuffle deck from a random one and almost never errs, which is why the total variation distance reads 1.000 for the first four shuffles. The 8.55 comes from the asymptotic formula; four shuffles fail because the count gives them away.

quiz.prompt: 賭場設備廠商的工程師跑了幾項檢查都正常，三位作者仍判定那台洗牌機不能用。兩邊的判準差在哪裡？
options: 工程師的那幾項檢查算錯了
機器裡的亂數產生器本身有偏差
幾項檢查各自只算一個統計量，全變異距離取的是所有檢驗裡的最大差距
十層的機器結構產生不出隨機排列
quiz.explain: 作者算出單次通過之後每個排列的機率，再換算成懂行的玩家逐張猜能猜中幾張：那台機器 9.5 張，洗好的牌 4.5 張，這份數字說服了廠商。事先挑好的幾項檢查全部通過，說明的只是那幾個統計量正常；距離取所有事件的最大差距，還沒有人想到的檢驗也在計算之內。

en.prompt: A casino supplier's engineers ran their own checks on a shuffling machine and saw nothing wrong; the three authors ruled it unusable. Where do the two standards differ?
options: The engineers' checks were miscalculated
The random number generator inside the machine was biased
Each check computes one statistic, while total variation takes the largest gap over every possible test
A ten-shelf mechanism cannot produce a random permutation
en.explain: The authors computed the probability of each permutation after a single pass, then converted it into cards a knowledgeable player guesses one at a time: 9.5 for the machine against 4.5 for a well-shuffled deck, and that figure persuaded the supplier. A fixed set of checks passing says only that those statistics look normal; the distance takes the largest gap over all events, tests nobody has thought of included.

right.statement: 洗七次之後，52 張牌的分佈與均勻分佈的全變異距離是 0.334；再洗一次減到 0.167。
right.why: 把數字連同它的距離一起講出來，讀者才知道 0.334 是什麼意思：任何一個檢驗，最多只能拿到三成三的優勢。

en.statement: After seven shuffles the total variation distance between the deck and the uniform distribution is 0.334; one more shuffle brings it to 0.167.
en.why: Quoting the number together with its distance tells the reader what 0.334 means: no test can do better than a 33 percent edge.

right.statement: 只要在意的是紅黑，六次之後分離距離是 0.317；問全副牌序，十二次仍有 0.278。
right.why: 同一副牌、同一個距離，答案隨問題改變。說「夠亂了」之前要先說清楚是為了什麼用途。

en.statement: If only the colours matter, separation distance is 0.317 after six shuffles; for the full order of the deck it is still 0.278 after twelve.
en.why: Same deck, same distance, different question. "Random enough" is only meaningful once the use is named.

right.statement: 這些結果算的是 Gilbert–Shannon–Reeds 模型下的洗牌，該文說明實驗顯示這個模型能描述人實際的洗法。
right.why: 結論的適用範圍等於模型的適用範圍。模型與人手之間的落差是實證問題，不是數學結果的一部分。

en.statement: These results are computed under the Gilbert-Shannon-Reeds model, which the paper reports to be a good description of how people actually shuffle.
en.why: A conclusion reaches exactly as far as its model does. Whether hands match the model is an empirical question, separate from the theorem.

wrong.claim: 洗六次不隨機，洗七次就隨機了。
wrong.why: 距離從 1 連續降到 0，第七次是 0.334、第十次 0.043，沒有任何一次讓它等於 0。把陡降讀成門檻，等於把一條曲線讀成一道開關。
wrong.instead: 寫「洗牌的混合程度在第五次到第八次之間急劇下降，第七次的距離是 0.334」。

en.claim: Six shuffles is not random; seven is.
en.why: The distance falls continuously from 1 towards 0 and never reaches it: 0.334 at seven, 0.043 at ten. Reading the steep part as a threshold turns a curve into a switch.
en.instead: Write that mixing drops sharply between the fifth and eighth shuffle, and that the distance at seven is 0.334.

wrong.why: 同一條公式給 32 張牌五到六次、104 張牌八到九次、312 張牌十一次以上；七次是 52 張牌的位置，隨 $\frac{3}{2}\log_2 n$ 移動。
wrong.instead: 先說牌堆有幾張，再引對應的數值。

en.claim: Seven shuffles is enough for any deck.
en.why: Seven belongs to 52 cards. The same formula gives five or six for 32 cards, eight or nine for 104, and eleven or more for 312, tracking (3/2) log2 n.
en.instead: State the deck size first, then quote the number that goes with it.

wrong.claim: 七次是這個問題的答案。
wrong.why: 以資訊量衡量，52 張牌洗五次剩 3.52% 的資訊、六次剩 0.92%，而且沒有陡降。該文自己的收尾是：兩種衡量哪一種更要緊，要看玩的是哪一種遊戲。距離換了，答案就換了。
wrong.instead: 講「在全變異距離下，第七次是 0.334；改以資訊量衡量，五次剩 3.52%、六次剩 0.92%」，把判準寫進句子裡。

en.claim: Seven is the answer to this question.
en.why: Measured by information, 3.52 percent remains after five shuffles and 0.92 percent after six, with no cut-off at all. The paper closes by saying that which measure matters more to gamblers and card players is presumably game dependent. Change the distance and the answer changes.
en.instead: Say "0.334 at seven under total variation; 3.52 percent of the information left at five and 0.92 percent at six", and keep the criterion inside the sentence.

wrong.claim: 幾項隨機性檢查都通過了，所以這台洗牌機沒問題。
wrong.why: 一組事先挑好的檢查通過，只說明這幾個統計量正常。同一台十層洗牌機通過了工程師自訂的檢查，卻讓懂行的玩家單次平均猜中 9.5 張，而洗好的牌是 4.5 張。
wrong.instead: 算距離，或算一個涵蓋所有檢驗的指標（例如最佳猜牌策略的期望猜中數），不要只列通過的檢查。

en.claim: It passed several randomness tests, so the machine is fine.
en.why: Passing a fixed set of tests says only that those statistics look normal. The ten-shelf machine passed the engineers' own tests while letting a knowledgeable player guess 9.5 cards per run, against 4.5 for a well-shuffled deck.
en.instead: Compute a distance, or a quantity that ranges over all tests such as the expected number of correct guesses under the best strategy.

misreadings.claim: 洗六次不隨機，洗七次就隨機了。
misreadings.why: 距離從 1 連續降到 0，第七次是 0.334、第十次 0.043，沒有任何一次讓它等於 0。把陡降讀成門檻，等於把一條曲線讀成一道開關。
misreadings.instead: 寫「洗牌的混合程度在第五次到第八次之間急劇下降，第七次的距離是 0.334」。

en.claim: Six shuffles is not random; seven is.
en.why: The distance falls continuously from 1 towards 0 and never reaches it: 0.334 at seven, 0.043 at ten. Reading the steep part as a threshold turns a curve into a switch.
en.instead: Write that mixing drops sharply between the fifth and eighth shuffle, and that the distance at seven is 0.334.

misreadings.why: 同一條公式給 32 張牌五到六次、104 張牌八到九次、312 張牌十一次以上；七次是 52 張牌的位置，隨 $\frac{3}{2}\log_2 n$ 移動。
misreadings.instead: 先說牌堆有幾張，再引對應的數值。

en.claim: Seven shuffles is enough for any deck.
en.why: Seven belongs to 52 cards. The same formula gives five or six for 32 cards, eight or nine for 104, and eleven or more for 312, tracking (3/2) log2 n.
en.instead: State the deck size first, then quote the number that goes with it.

cutoff-phenomenon.oneLine: 距離幾乎不動地貼著 1，到某個次數附近才在很短的區間內掉到接近 0。
cutoff-phenomenon.example: 52 張牌洗前四次距離都是 1.000，第五次 0.924，第六次 0.614，第七次 0.334，第八次 0.167。

en.oneLine: The distance sits at 1, then falls almost all the way to 0 within a short window around a critical number of steps.
en.example: Four riffle shuffles of 52 cards leave the distance at 1.000; then come 0.924, 0.614, 0.334 and 0.167.

riffle-shuffle.oneLine: 把一副牌分成兩疊、讓兩疊交錯落下的洗法，也是撲克牌最常見的洗法。
riffle-shuffle.example: 52 張牌照這種洗法洗七次，與均勻分佈的全變異距離降到 0.334；洗四次以下，牌堆最多只有 16 段遞增序列，一眼就分得出來。

en.oneLine: Splitting a deck into two packets and letting them fall interleaved, the way cards are usually shuffled.
en.example: Seven such shuffles of 52 cards bring the total variation distance down to 0.334; four or fewer leave at most 16 rising sequences, which is easy to spot.

total-variation-distance.oneLine: 兩個機率分佈之間，在同一個事件上機率差距的最大值。
total-variation-distance.example: 有人瞄到一副洗好的牌的底牌。「底牌是那一張」這個事件，在均勻分佈下的機率是 1/52，在他知道之後是 1，兩者的全變異距離因此是 51/52。

en.oneLine: The largest gap between two probability distributions on any single event.
en.example: Someone glimpses the bottom card of a shuffled deck. The event “the bottom card is that one” has probability 1/52 under the uniform distribution and 1 under theirs, so the total variation distance is 51/52.
